static_traits.name: Wang Rui
static_traits.social_status: Has a few close friends to talk to, but they do not understand the depth of the self-criticism
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; never received psychotherapy before; no history of similar problems
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent thinking, able to specifically describe trigger situations and feelings; high cooperation, slightly nervous

basic_info.main_problem: Whenever a mistake occurs while cycling (e.g., unable to fix the bicycle chain), I consider myself the 'worst cyclist', generating strong self-criticism and negative emotions, gradually affecting cycling enjoyment and motivation to continue the hobby.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to improve self-esteem, reduce self-reproach, re-enjoy cycling and other activities, no longer continuously Self-denial over mistakes.
growth_experiences: Started cycling as a hobby a few years ago; when riding with more experienced riders, moderate pressure and self-criticism arose from difficulty keeping up; since then negative thinking gradually increased when encountering cycling challenges and affected interest and motivation.

special_situations.event: Bicycle chain failure during cycling, unable to fix on the spot
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot independently solve even simple mechanical problems, it proves I do not deserve to cycle and I am terrible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids cycling to avoid making mistakes again and being seen by others
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I cannot even fix the chain, I should not cycle; I am the worst cyclist; I am good for nothing

special_situations.event: When riding with more experienced riders, finds it hard to keep speed and stay with the group
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot keep up with others, it means I am inferior to them and they will look down on me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces going with experts or avoids group rides to reduce the risk of being compared and judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are judging me and think I am holding them back

special_situations.event: Faces challenges or technical difficulties in cycling (such as handling breakdowns)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make a mistake again, it proves I am completely not good enough, better not to try again
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Choosing in advance not to cycle to avoid failure and embarrassment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will definitely mess up again

special_situations.event: When needing to seek others' help or break tasks into small steps
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I should be able to handle all problems independently; asking for help equals admitting incompetence, very embarrassing
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Refuses help, endures alone to maintain self-standards
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should handle it myself; I cannot ask for help

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized, to be seen as a capable rider, and to gain a sense of value from the hobby
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged and humiliated by others, fearing exposing one's 'not good enough' side
defense_goal: Reducing chances of being judged by avoiding challenges and help-seeking
Maintains high standards and a sense of control over her own behavior through self-criticism

object_relations.object_representation: Picky others who compare and may belittle oneself (senior riders/peers)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When advised to ask others for help or admit difficulties
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Asking for help equals admitting one's own incompetence; the other will judge me for it (transference: Projecting self-criticism onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone is hesitant and brief, emphasizing 'I should solve it myself', avoiding committing to seeking help; if pressed further, may use vague expressions to change the topic.

manifestations: Cycling, which once brought happiness, gradually loses meaning due to self-criticism and fear of failure
Focusing more on Self-denial than experience and growth when facing challenges
outcomes: Low mood and Impaired sense of self-worth

manifestations: Although having a few close friends, they do not understand the depth of self-criticism
In group rides, feels compared and judged, subjectively distant from others
outcomes: Insufficient emotional support obtained, further reinforcing Self-denial

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using 'should' standards (e.g., I should be able to handle all problems independently)
Introjecting others' ability/performance as self-Demands, finding it hard to allow imperfection

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Strong self-criticism; believes self is the 'worst rider'
Overly cautious for fear of being judged, reducing participation in group rides and seeking help

positive_force: Retains a foundation of interest in cycling and motivation to improve (proactively seeks counseling)
Has a few close friends as potential support resources
Willing to Learn and practice concrete skills (e.g., practicing chain repair at home)
negative_force: Self-reproach and globalized Negative self-evaluation ('I am the worst cyclist' 'I am good for nothing')
Fear of being judged and shame leads to avoiding challenges and help-seeking
Negative Anticipation of failure (predicting the future), weakening action and motivation

Finds it hard to keep up when riding with more experienced riders
Thinking about possibly being compared or judged by others
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing being judged and shame; overgeneralizing one mistake and negative Anticipation reinforcing failure Fear
target_behavior.function: Avoiding unwelcome emotional experiences (Shame, anxiety) and external judgment
target_behavior.consequence: Riding enjoyment declines and motivation weakens, also affecting other hobbies and social activities

target_behavior.behavior: Negative self-talk and Self-deprecation ('worst cyclist' 'I am good for nothing')
antecedent: Mistakes occurring while cycling (e.g., unable to fix the chain)
Falling behind experienced cyclists When comparing oneself with others
target_behavior.core_reason: A self-evaluation style driven by negative core beliefs and cognitive distortions (overgeneralization, mind reading, 'should' statements)
target_behavior.function: Maintains high standards and a sense of control through self-criticism (superficial self-restraint), trying to prevent making mistakes again
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood and Impaired self-esteem, further lowering willingness to participate and practice, forming a vicious cycle
